scope: Publish two long first-person silver five-finger robot-arm RV2V comparisons with disclosed tabletop source-background restoration
summary: Two complete bimanual source videos were converted with four full-stream JoyAI candidates each; seed 101 plus full-timeline background projection is published for the 35.917-second tabletop case and direct seed 73 for the 40.167-second device/cable case.
evidence: The browser comparisons decode completely as H.264 High, yuv420p, 1280x360, 24 FPS with exact 862- and 964-frame timelines.
The selected direct model edits measured 113.316 seconds at 7.634 FPS and 128.609 seconds at 7.534 FPS on the recorded two-A800 service.
The tabletop source-state projection preserves candidate pixels exactly in the robot union, restores safe source pixels exactly, and passes the recorded flow non-regression gates.
The public package includes the exact source-aligned reference images, prompts, source hashes, model revisions, media hashes, timing, and claim boundary.
lessons: Long first-person RV2V can run as one bounded causal stream without window seams, but visual quality remains distinct from physical validity.
Dynamic non-robot detail is better restored from the corresponding source frame than from a static clean plate, provided both source-human and candidate-robot support are protected.
Reference images must match first-person handedness, wrist entry, scale, and initial grasp rather than using a generic front-facing robot image.
limitations: Timeline review was sampled rather than a claim of manual per-pixel acceptance for every frame.
Thin cables and robot fingers overlap repeatedly in the device clip and remain vulnerable to local sticking, deformation, or flicker.
The outputs contain no metric-depth, kinematic, force, sensor-contact, or real-robot evidence.
next_actions: Obtain final user review of the prepared GitHub diff and browser preview before pushing main.
Add a dedicated lower-resolution and one-step benchmark before making any realtime claim.
